- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- If sentiment drops sharply (e.g., 0.00 or negative) after a spike, model often overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% below recent peak.  
- After a strong upward move (e.g., >70.00), model frequently overcorrects downward; apply a 1–2% upward bias to offset mean reversion.  
- If history shows rapid decline (e.g., 3+ consecutive drops), model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid underreaction.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture sentiment-driven momentum; adjust forecast to align with sentiment trend (e.g., if sentiment >0.7, forecast should trend up).  
- If sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.33–0.67), model tends to average out; use median of recent 5–7 days as baseline for correction.  
- When sentiment is 0.00 for 3+ consecutive days, model underperforms; add 1–2% to forecast to counteract pessimism.  
- Model often lags sentiment shifts by 1–3 days; adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead to match sentiment direction.
